html:
The Ateshgah of Baku is a fire temple at Surakhani, east of Baku, built in the 1700s by Hindu and Zoroastrian traders and pilgrims from India around natural gas vents that burned without ceasing.

The Absheron peninsula's eternal flames, fed by the same oil and gas that later made Baku rich, drew worshippers of fire for centuries and gave Azerbaijan its name of land of fire. Indian merchants on the caravan routes between India and Russia built the pentagonal courtyard of cells around a central altar, with inscriptions in Sanskrit, Punjabi and Persian. Pilgrims left after the 1880s as oil drilling drained the gas, and the natural flame went out in 1969; it is now fed by a pipe. Many link it with Zoroastrianism.
sum: The Ateshgah of Baku is a fire temple at Surakhani, east of Baku, built in the 1700s by Hindu and Zoroastrian traders and pilgrims from India around natural gas vents that burned without ceasing.
